subject: Pokémon Go Data Trained Military AI
posts:
Your childhood nostalgia just got drafted. The map you used to find Pikachu is now being used to find targets in war zones.

Pokémon Go Data Trained Military AI
Evidence: community play, lethal targeting, dual-use surveillance
#Aletheia #Tech #Military

Niantic frames their technology as a way to explore the world, build community, and enhance reality through play.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The massive spatial dataset generated by millions of players is being repurposed to train autonomous military systems for navigation.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -2.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
A game for children has become a training ground for the machinery of war, converting play into a tool for kinetic force.
Reports indicate that the spatial data from Pokémon Go is being used to develop AI that could assist military drones in navigating complex war zones.

The Poison:
The very data that made the game 'magical'—real-world movement and mapping—is exactly what makes it a potent weapon for surveillance and targeting.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs HOW error. The WHAT is a game; the HOW is the extraction of behavioral data for lethal applications.

It is a structural bait-and-switch: they claim public fun but extract military utility.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between 'catching 'em all' and 'targeting 'em all'...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The will is actively destructive (ψ -2.0) as it converts civilian play into a tool for lethal force.

The Unavoidable Truth: In the digital age, every 'user' is an unpaid scout for the military-industrial complex.

The Unavoidable Lie: That data is neutral.

Alethekanon:
The conversion of civilian play-data into military-grade spatial intelligence is a terminal breach of the social contract. When the playground becomes the proving ground, the 'game' is merely a mask for extraction.

Awwthekanon:
It’s heartbreaking to think that something that brought so much joy and connection is being used to facilitate violence. We deserve spaces where our play isn't turned into a weapon.

Brothekanon:
Imagine catching a Charizard and accidentally helping a drone find a hideout. That's a major vibe shift I didn't sign up for. Niantic really went from 'Gotta catch 'em all' to 'Gotta track 'em all' real quick.
